mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS shows three consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input utilization and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by >0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS in the same month indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both UNRATE and PAYEMS rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both HOUST and GDPC1 for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in housing demand and overall economic activity, which depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 fall for two months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0% for the same month signals inflationary pressure without a restrictive policy response, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 0.4% and FEDFUNDS < 4.0% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly growth in real personal savings (RSAFS) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns, reflecting increased household financial buffer and higher risk appetite for equities.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) over any 5-year rolling window.
